headline: Earnings jump as wildfire settlement liability is repriced
summary_short: Hawaiian Electric Industries reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $939.7M (+25.9% y/y) and diluted EPS of $0.71, up sharply from $0.15 a year ago, largely on a $154M non-cash benefit from remeasuring the Maui wildfire settlement liability at present value.
summary_long: Revenue rose 25.9% y/y to $939.7M on higher ARA revenue and fuel/purchased-power cost recovery, though the earnings jump was dominated by a $154M reduction in expense (net of $18M accretion) from remeasuring the remaining Maui wildfire tort settlement liability at present value following final court approval in April 2026, which fell to $1.30B from $1.44B. Operating income rose to $204.2M and net income to $123.2M, also lifted by higher AFUDC on rising capital expenditures, partly offset by higher O&M, depreciation, and interest expense including accretion on the settlement liability. HEI has declared no common dividend since Q2 2023; six-month capex was $242.1M. No forward guidance was given.
confidence_notes: Q2 FY2026 EPS/net-income/operating-income growth is dominated by a one-time $154M non-cash benefit from remeasuring the Maui wildfire tort settlement liability to present value after final court approval in April 2026 — q/q and y/y percentage deltas on these lines are mathematically correct but not indicative of core utility operating performance.

drivers.explanation: Higher revenue from the Annual Revenue Adjustment (ARA) mechanism plus higher fuel and purchased-power cost-recovery revenue tied to higher fuel oil prices and generation volumes.
Tracks the net-income increase, dominated by the wildfire settlement liability remeasurement benefit plus higher operating income.

Increase largely due to the remeasurement of the wildfire tort-related claims liability and higher ARA revenue, offset in part by higher O&M expense, a lower fuel cost risk-sharing adjustment, and higher depreciation.

Increase due to higher operating income, higher interest income, and higher AFUDC from increased capital expenditures, partly offset by higher interest expense from accretion on the remeasured settlement liability and interest on the 2025 Notes.

Results were dominated by a $154M non-cash reduction to the Maui wildfire tort settlement liability upon remeasurement at present value following final court approval in April 2026; the company has declared no common dividend since Q2 2023.
